title: CSS organization, naming, reusable components
learningObjectives: Explain css organization, naming, reusable components and use modern CSS features responsibly.

understand.concept: Maintainable CSS uses consistent naming, sensible file or layer organisation, reusable component rules, and clear ownership of design tokens. Avoid unnecessary specificity escalation and unexplained overrides. CSS methodologies can help teams agree on boundaries without being mandatory.
understand.whyItMatters: As a project grows, duplicated rules and cascade conflicts become harder to debug. Consistent organisation reduces accidental coupling and makes changes safer.
understand.analogy: A stylesheet is like a shared workshop: labels, tool locations, and repeatable patterns help everyone work without confusion.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS parsing, specificity, and feature support follow the relevant browser standards.

explain.narrative: The component uses one clear class boundary and keeps its declarations together. The class naming convention can be expanded as the component system grows.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for maintainable modern CSS?
options: Use clear rules, appropriate fallbacks, and inspect computed behaviour
Use the newest feature everywhere without checking support
Increase specificity whenever a style does not apply
questions.answer: Use clear rules, appropriate fallbacks, and inspect computed behaviour
questions.explanation: Maintainability depends on clarity, support-aware enhancement, and understanding the cascade.
